neutral_facts.value: The deceased was part of a bus traveling through a junction where an unlawful assembly of individuals from opposing political parties had gathered. The assembly's common object was to attack any rival party supporter. The deceased was attacked and killed during this incident. The accused were part of the assembly and were involved in the attack, with some individuals using sticks and a knife to inflict injuries. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts and medical evidence to establish the incident and the involvement of the accused in the unlawful assembly.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused were part of an unlawful assembly with a common object to attack any rival party supporter, and that the deceased was killed in the attack. The evidence of PW3 and PW4 was crucial in establishing the common object and the involvement of the accused.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the High Court erred in not considering the evidence of PW4, which could be used for corroboration. They also claimed that the accused did not have a common object to commit murder and that the prosecution failed to prove the common object of the unlawful assembly.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the mere presence in an unlawful assembly may vicariously fasten criminal liability under Section 149 IPC, and that the conduct of the accused determines whether they shared the common object of the assembly.
